# Introduction

## Prerequisites

* R library ape
* msms.jar 
* PopPlaner.jar

## Coalescent approximation:
Moving from trees mainting the ancestry (remember our zigge-zagge trees) to more pretty trees. The idea is that the only peaces of interesting information are the time between coalescent events and the topology

![](../pics/ca.png)

\clearpage


The coalescent approximation is based on the following insights:

* Populations are large and only some k lineages are viewed; the probability that more than two lineages coalesce at the same time can be neglected
* the process of generating a topology can be separated from generating the branch length, i.e.: first a random topology can be generated and than random branch length (exponential distribution) can be drawn.

**major advantage of coalescent approximation: very fast**

## implementing a coalescent approximation
### requirements
**obtaining a subset of a vector excluding some elements **
```{r}
a<-10:20
b<-a[-2]
b
```

** Random exponentially distributed values**
```{r}
# exponential distribution: mean = 1/rate
# ie the higher the rate, the lower the mean
hist(rexp(500,rate=10))
hist(rexp(500,rate=1))

```


```{r}
coaltree <- function(n) {
  # many thanks to Thomas Taus for sharing his brilliant code!
  
  # initate the nodes; branch lengths are all 0
  nodes <- rep(0, times=n)
  names(nodes) <- 1:n
  
  # simulate one coalescent event after the other
  for(i in seq(1, n-1)) {
    ncount <- length(nodes) # node count
    
    # pick random nodes to merge
    tomerge <- sample(ncount, size=2)
    
    # random branch length; exponential distribution
    bl <- rexp(1, rate=ncount*(ncount-1)/2)
    
    # get length of the two nodes
    left <- nodes[tomerge[1]]
    right <- nodes[tomerge[2]]
    
    # length difference between the two nodes that should be merged
    deltaleft <- if(right > left) right-left else 0
    deltaright <- if(left > right) left-right else 0
    
    # new node name;
    # ie. names of the two merged nodes
    # plus the branch lengths
    # = Newick
    cnode <- paste("(", names(left), ":", bl+deltaleft, ",", names(right), ":", bl+deltaright, ")", sep="")
    
    # remove the two merged nodes
    nodes <- nodes[-tomerge]
    
    #add the new composite node
    # first the length
    nodes <- c(nodes, max(bl+left, bl+right))
    # than the name
    names(nodes)[length(nodes)] <- cnode
  }
  
  # add semicolon, a Newick requirement
  return(paste0(names(nodes), ";"))
}
# compute the tree
newicktree <- coaltree(10)
newicktree

# plot the tree
ct<-read.tree(text=newicktree)
plot(ct)
```

# msms (ms mit selektion)
Coalescent simulations with selection

## Minimal call of msms

```{bash eval=FALSE}
java -jar msms.jar sampleCount repeats -t theta
```

* sampleCount: number of DNA sequences
* repeats: how often should the simulations be repeated for the given set of parameters
* theta: amount of polymorphism $\theta=4N_e\mu$ Interestingly we would get the same amount of polymorphism by either increasing the mutation rate or the effective population size.

## Influence of demography

### Growing population

```{bash eval=FALSE}
# growth -G growthRate_alpha
java -jar msms.jar 10 1 -t 5 -T -G 1.5
```

* $N=Ne^{-\alpha t}$
* alpha positive expanding
* alpha negative shrinking

```{r echo=FALSE}
tree<-"((2:0.00935,7:0.00935):0.56482,(8:0.45675,(((1:0.02629,4:0.02629):0.22537,((9:0.00680,10:0.00680):0.12251,(3:0.05094,5:0.05094):0.07837):0.12236):0.06624,6:0.31791):0.13884):0.11742);"
plot(read.tree(text=tree))
```

* Whats the difference?
* How is the expected pattern of polymorphism changing? 
* Where do you expect more singletons?


### Bottleneck


```{bash eval=FALSE}
java -jar msms.jar 10 1 -t 5 -T -I 1 10 -en 0.2 1 0.3 -en 0.4 1 1.0
```

Questions and tasks

* -I demes samples
* -en bottlenecktime demenumber fraction_popsize
* -en 0.2 1 0.3 bottleneck starting at time 0.2; size = 30% of original population
* -en 0.4 1 1.0 end of bottleneck at time 0.4
* Play with different bottleneck times and sizes

```{r echo=TRUE}
tree="((((2:0.00689,5:0.00689):0.05246,1:0.05936):0.13163,(7:0.07542,4:0.07542):0.11557):1.72711,(6:0.10136,(8:0.09976,((3:0.01124,9:0.01124):0.02080,10:0.03204):0.06771):0.00160):1.81675);"
```

## Selection ##

```{r eval=FALSE}
java -jar msms.jar 10 1 -t 5 -r 500 20 -SAA 2000 -SaA 1000 -N 10000 -SF 0 -Sp .5
```

* -r recombinationrate recombinationsites
* -SAA selection coefficient of homozygous beneficial genotype
* -SAa selection coefficient of heterozygous allele
* -N population size
* -SF time since fixation
* -Sp position of selected allele on a scale from 0 to 1. In case of 0.5 selected allele is at the middle of the simulated loci


```{bash eval=FALSE}
java -jar msms.jar 10 1 -t 5 -T -SAA 300 -SaA 200 -N 10000 -SF 0 -Sp .5
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
tree="(3:0.04612,((((4:0.04053,9:0.04053):0.00082,6:0.04135):0.00173,(5:0.01006,8:0.01006):0.03302):0.00163,((1:0.00498,2:0.00498):0.03826,(7:0.04122,10:0.04122):0.00202):0.00147):0.00141);"
plot(read.tree(text=tree))
```

**How is this site frequency spectrum going to look like?**

* compute the site frequency spectrum of a simple neutral coalescent (20 sites); whats the influence of theta?
* compare it to a site frequency spectrum using a scenary with selection (eg.: -ms 20 1000 -t 100 -r 500 20 -SAA 2000 -SaA 1000 -N 10000 -SF 0 -Sp .5)

* whats the influence of SF and the position of the selected site?

* can you mimic the signature of selection using a migration scenario?
